question: You are working with a nursing assistant on your team. Which of these tasks is safe and appropriate to delegate to them?

options.A: Assisting a stable patient with morning bath and hygiene
options.B: Assessing a newly admitted patient with chest pain
options.C: Administering intravenous medications to a critical patient
options.D: Changing the comprehensive nursing care plan

explanation: Correct! Nursing assistants are wonderful helpers trained for basic comfort measures like hygiene, while medications and assessments need your professional skills. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why must a researcher carefully explain how they chose their participants (sample selection)?

options.A: To make the research budget look much smaller than it is
options.B: To hide the identities of the nurses working on the ward
options.C: So others understand who was studied and can judge if results are fair
options.D: To ensure that only wealthy patients take part in the study

explanation: Being transparent about your participants builds trust and shows everyone that your results are reliable and unbiased. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is a major home hazard that can cause older adults to fall?

options.A: Having too many windows in the bedroom
options.B: Loose carpets and inadequate lighting
options.C: Using electric fans during warm weather
options.D: Brightly painted walls in the hallway

explanation: Simple things like dim hallways or loose rugs are major tripping hazards. Home safety assessments are a key part of community nursing care for the elderly! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is a key nursing duty during the post-disaster recovery phase?

options.A: Monitoring for delayed health issues like infectious disease outbreaks
options.B: Stopping all documentation of past emergency responses
options.C: Discontinuing all community health education programs permanently
options.D: Closing down local clinics indefinitely

explanation: You got it! Even after the dust settles, crowded conditions and dirty water pose major risks, so nurses must stay alert for disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h8)

question: What is the best way to explain home care instructions to a patient with low health literacy?

options.A: Relying entirely on written pamphlets without verbal explanation
options.B: Using simple, plain language and asking the client to repeat instructions
options.C: Speaking in complex clinical terminology to sound professional
options.D: Handing the client a dense medical textbook to read overnight

explanation: You got it! Plain words plus the teach-back method (asking them to explain it back to you) guarantees they truly understand their treatment. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h4)

question: What emotional feeling do patients adjusting to a new stoma most commonly experience?

options.A: Complete indifference to physical changes
options.B: Immediate excitement to rush back to work
options.C: Angry behavior toward medical staff
options.D: Body image disturbance and anxiety

explanation: Spot on. Adjusting to a changed body appearance and worrying about leaks or smells can easily cause stress and emotional upset. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h7)

question: A ward manager is told to cut costs, but management won't let her approve any purchase orders. Which key management rule is being broken?

options.A: Traditional authority supersedes expert authority
options.B: Delegation must transfer ultimate legal accountability
options.C: Power must always exceed formal authority
options.D: Authority and responsibility must be balanced

explanation: Makes total sense, right? You can't give someone a heavy task (responsibility) without giving them the power (authority) to make it happen! [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h3)

question: What is the role of a neurotransmitter at a synapse?

options.A: To physically connect the dendrite of one cell to the axon of another
options.B: To chemically bridge the gap and transmit the signal to the next cell
options.C: To generate the original resting membrane potential
options.D: To insulate the axon with a protective fatty layer

explanation: Because electrical signals cannot cross the synaptic cleft, neurotransmitters carry the message chemically across the space. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h6)

question: When starting a heart failure patient on a new beta-blocker, what is the safest way to begin?

options.A: Give the drug only when the patient has chest pain
options.B: Start with a very low dose and increase it gradually
options.C: Give a high loading dose to get quick protection
options.D: Stop all other heart failure medications immediately

explanation: Exactly! Because beta-blockers can temporarily slow things down too much when first introduced, our golden nursing rule is always: 'start low and go slow.' [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h3)

question: For weak, frail patients, why do we recommend small, frequent meals instead of three big ones?

options.A: They prevent the patient from feeling overwhelmed and reduce fatigue during eating.
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any fiber in the diet.
options.C: They stop the stomach from producing normal digestive acids.
options.D: They guarantee that the patient will consume twice as many calories.

explanation: Eating a huge plate of food can exhaust a frail patient. Smaller, tasty portions throughout the day make eating feel manageable and less tiring. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following best describes inter-sectoral collaboration in immunization?

options.A: Partnering with schools, religious bodies, and local leaders to boost coverage
options.B: Leaving all public health work entirely to the central government
options.C: Working exclusively with doctors inside major hospital wards
options.D: Buying vaccines from international suppliers without local input

explanation: Inter-sectoral collaboration brings different community groups together to work toward shared public health goals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h7)

question: What is the main way typical antipsychotics work in the brain, causing both their main effects and many side effects?

options.A: Stimulation of GABA receptors in the cortex
options.B: Enhancement of serotonin reuptake
options.C: Strong blockade of dopamine D2 receptors
options.D: Inhibition of monoamine oxidase enzymes

explanation: Typical antipsychotics love to tightly bind and block D2 dopamine receptors. This strong blockade stops the psychosis, but it's also why movement side effects happen. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h3)

question: A patient is isolated from her family, constantly insulted, and threatened with losing her children if she disobeys. What type of abuse is this?

options.A: Accidental domestic stress
options.B: Emotional and psychological abuse
options.C: Harmful traditional practices
options.D: Physical violence only

explanation: Threats, insults, and forced isolation aim to break down a person's self-esteem, which defines psychological abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h2)

question: What is the name of the most common expectorant you'll see in everyday pharmacy practice?

options.A: Diphenhydramine
options.B: Salbutamol
options.C: Guaifenesin
options.D: Dextromethorphan

explanation: That's it! Guaifenesin is the go-to active ingredient in almost all chest congestion syrups you see on the shelves. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of activated charcoal when given for something a patient swallowed?

options.A: To neutralize stomach acid and prevent internal bleeding
options.B: To bind toxins in the gut and prevent them from entering the blood
options.C: To coat the throat and protect it from corrosive chemicals
options.D: To cause immediate vomiting and empty the stomach contents

explanation: Activated charcoal acts like a tiny sponge in the stomach! It grabs onto the toxins so they pass safely out of the body instead of entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T10#GNS125_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which type of cancer starts in the bone marrow and doesn't form solid lumps or tumors?

options.A: Melanoma
options.B: Sarcoma
options.C: Leukemia
options.D: Carcinoma

explanation: Leukemia affects our blood-forming tissues, sending lots of abnormal white blood cells into circulation instead of forming a solid tumor. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h2)

question: Which sign is most typical in a patient who has damage to Broca's area?

options.A: Inability to hear or recognize spoken words from others
options.B: Trouble speaking fluent words despite understanding language
options.C: Complete paralysis of all four limbs on the right side
options.D: Total loss of long-term memory about childhood events

explanation: This is expressive aphasia: the patient usually knows what they want to say in their head, but getting the words out is the struggle. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T10#GNS211_U3_T10_h5)

question: An injured survivor of an assault arrives at your facility. What is your very first clinical priority?

options.A: Conducting a detailed psychological interview
options.B: Filing mandatory police incident reports
options.C: Collecting forensic swabs and clothing fibers
options.D: Stabilizing life-threatening physical injuries

explanation: Saving a life and stabilizing the patient always comes first before collecting evidence or paperwork. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h4)

question: Who primarily handled the care of sick family members in most ancient households?

options.A: Professional monastic orders
options.B: Government-certified physicians
options.C: Women within the home
options.D: Trained military nurses

explanation: Before formal institutions, caring for the sick was mainly a domestic duty performed by female family members. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: A student looks at a slide where bone-building cells (osteoblasts) are laying down matrix directly into a tissue sheet. What process is happening?

options.A: Intramembranous ossification
options.B: Interstitial bone growth
options.C: Endochondral ossification
options.D: Articular cartilage repair

explanation: Spot on! When bone forms straight from a connective tissue sheet without a cartilage stage, it's called intramembranous ossification. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T1#GNS121_U3_T1_h2)

question: A nurse wants to study past unconscious ICU dreams, but no records exist. Which research requirement is missing?

options.A: Clinical significance
options.B: Availability of data
options.C: Ethical clearance
options.D: Personal interest

explanation: If the information you need doesn't exist or can't be gathered, you won't be able to carry out that specific study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the main goal of civil service rules for government workers?

options.A: To replace the professional nursing curriculum set by the council
options.B: To provide a standard framework for employment and administrative conduct
options.C: To dictate the specific clinical medications nurses can prescribe
options.D: To determine the personal income tax rates for civil servants

explanation: Civil service rules are simply the workplace guidelines that keep public institutions organized. They tell everyone what is expected regarding job terms and daily conduct! [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h1)

question: A patient with newly fitted dentures is struggling to eat regular hospital food. What diet modification should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: A salt-restricted diet to control blood pressure
options.B: A soft diet to ease chewing discomfort
options.C: A high-fiber diet to stimulate digestion
options.D: A clear liquid diet for complete bowel rest

explanation: New dentures often cause sore gums, making a soft diet necessary until the patient adjusts. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h2)

question: Which group is often most vulnerable during a disaster due to reliance on continuous care or medical equipment?

options.A: Office workers
options.B: The elderly
options.C: Store owners
options.D: Young adults

explanation: Correct! Older adults often have chronic health needs and rely heavily on steady electricity and support that can fail during a crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h3)

question: According to the IASC intervention pyramid, which tier represents specialized mental health care given by professionals?

options.A: Tier 4
options.B: Tier 1
options.C: Tier 2
options.D: Tier 3

explanation: Tier 4 sits right at the top of the IASC pyramid. It's where specialists step in with clinical treatments for patients who need deeper care. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T4#GNS314_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is a major risk associated with using social media networks during a fast-moving crisis?

options.A: The rapid spread of unverified rumors and false information
options.B: High costs charged to citizens for reading emergency alerts
options.C: The complete inability to transmit text messages or pictures
options.D: Government blockades that stop all communication instantly

explanation: Social media allows anyone to post instantly, which can lead to panic if false reports circulate before officials verify them. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why do nurse researchers use random sampling when picking study participants?

options.A: It ensures that every participant receives the new treatment.
options.B: It completely eliminates all human errors during data entry.
options.C: It helps the sample represent the wider population accurately.
options.D: It reduces the total financial cost of running the hospital.

explanation: Exactly! Random sampling gives everyone an equal chance, making sure your small group is a fair mini-version of the larger population. Brilliant thinking! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the gallbladder?

options.A: To manufacture digestive enzymes
options.B: To store and concentrate bile
options.C: To filter red blood cells
options.D: To absorb digested fats

explanation: The gallbladder acts as a reservoir that holds bile made by the liver until it is needed for fat digestion. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does a psychiatric nurse help reduce community stigma regarding mental illness?

options.A: By keeping all psychiatric diagnoses strictly hidden from the public
options.B: By admitting every stressed individual into a secure hospital ward
options.C: By telling patients to ignore their symptoms and stay busy
options.D: By educating families that mental conditions are treatable medical illnesses

explanation: Education helps remove shame by teaching the community that mental health challenges are medical issues, just like physical conditions. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is a major goal of teaching a patient who experiences dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: To convince the patient to avoid all physical movement during menstruation
options.B: To ensure the patient stops taking all prescribed medications immediately
options.C: To empower the patient with self-care techniques and pain management strategies
options.D: To discourage the patient from discussing menstrual health with relatives

explanation: Correct! Good education gives patients practical tools like heat therapy and proper medication use so they feel in control. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h8)

question: How should a nurse manager approach an appraisal where an employee shows weak clinical skills?

options.A: Cut the employee's salary without any prior discussion
options.B: Ignore the issue so the employee does not feel bad
options.C: Use it as an opportunity to provide constructive feedback and training
options.D: Publicly announce the mistakes during a general hospital meeting

explanation: Appraisals should identify gaps so managers can arrange mentoring or education to support the nurse. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is the main feature of quantitative data collection?

options.A: They rely entirely on the researcher's personal feelings and intuition
options.B: They avoid using any structured tools or standardized checklists
options.C: They produce numerical data that can be measured and analyzed statistically
options.D: They focus exclusively on recording long, emotional personal stories

explanation: Quantitative data is all about quantities and numbers that you can run statistics on. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h3)

question: What is the main worry with osteoporosis that nurses must look out for?

options.A: Severe bacterial inflammation spreading throughout the bone marrow
options.B: Excessive mineral deposition causing bones to become overly rigid
options.C: Abnormal hardening of the joints preventing any physical movement
options.D: Decreased bone mass and density leading to a high risk of fractures

explanation: Osteoporosis makes bones porous and fragile, meaning even a small bump can lead to a painful fracture. Great clinical insight! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h8)

question: How do Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) help fight HIV?

options.A: They dissolve the fatty outer envelope of the virus
options.B: They act as faulty building blocks to stop viral DNA creation
options.C: They physically block the outer cell membrane receptors
options.D: They destroy mature viral particles circulating in the plasma

explanation: Brilliant! NRTIs act like fake Lego pieces. When the virus tries to build its DNA, it grabs the fake piece and the process grinds to a halt. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h2)

question: Which of these actions is a direct violation of patient data privacy?

options.A: Logging out of an electronic health record terminal when finished
options.B: Discussing lab results inside a private physician consultation room
options.C: Sharing your personal computer login password with a colleague
options.D: Shredding physical notes that contain identifying patient details

explanation: Never share your password! It breaks system security and leaves you legally responsible if someone messes up a patient record using your account. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h7)

question: How much extra stockinette length should generally be cut beyond the planned cast area?

options.A: At least 5 meters for safety
options.B: 10 to 15 centimeters at each end
options.C: Exactly 2 millimeters total
options.D: No extra length at all

explanation: Leaving 10 to 15 centimeters of extra stockinette at both ends is necessary so the edges can be folded back over the cast later. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h5)

question: How soon can a person's fertility return after an abortion procedure?

options.A: After exactly six months
options.B: Not for at least two years
options.C: As early as two weeks
options.D: Only after menopause begins

explanation: Surprise! Ovulation can bounce back in as little as two weeks. That's why talking about family planning early is so crucial before she leaves the clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h5)

question: How should a nurse best approach diet education for a patient going home with a new health condition?

options.A: Assume they already know basics from TV
options.B: Focus only on foods they cannot eat
options.C: Tailor teaching to their lifestyle and culture
options.D: Hand out a complex medical textbook to read

explanation: You got it! Teaching works best when it fits the patient's daily life, culture, and personal background. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to give rescue breaths too fast or with too much force?

options.A: It can force air into the stomach and lead to vomiting
options.B: It immediately collapses both lungs due to high pressure
options.C: It causes the patient's heart rate to drop dangerously low
options.D: It forces blood backward into the jugular veins

explanation: Easy does it with breaths! Blowing too hard opens up the stomach instead of the lungs, which can cause the patient to vomit and complicate things. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is keeping accurate records of swab counts so important for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: It provides legal protection and proves adherence to safety standards
options.B: It replaces the need to count out loud in the theater
options.C: It allows the hospital to buy fewer supplies next year
options.D: It is only required for hospital billing departments

explanation: Good paperwork is your best backup! Clear records show you followed all safety rules and protect you legally. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)

question: What are the temporary folds inside the stomach that flatten out when you eat a big meal called?

options.A: Haustra
options.B: Microvilli
options.C: Villi
options.D: Rugae

explanation: Rugae are like little accordion folds in the stomach lining. They let the stomach stretch safely when you enjoy a heavy meal! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T3#GNS121_U1_T3_h2)

question: What must be obtained before starting data collection with human participants in a study?

options.A: A commercial sponsor
options.B: Surgical clearance
options.C: A patent for a new drug
options.D: Ethical approval

explanation: Patient safety and rights always come first. Ethical approval ensures your study is safe and respects human dignity. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h5)

question: An educator wants to teach sterile gloving in a rural clinic with zero computers. Which factor will most strongly limit their choice of teaching methods?

options.A: The time of day
options.B: Student political opinions
options.C: Available resources
options.D: The age of the school principal

explanation: You have to work with what you have! If computers and advanced tools aren't there, the instructor has to rely on practical demonstrations with available supplies. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h6)

question: What regulatory body guides the professional practice and scope of nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Pharmacists Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria sets the legal boundaries and professional standards for all nursing practice in the country. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T2#GNS125_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary physiological defect in Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Temporary glucose intolerance during pregnancy
options.B: Target cell resistance to normal insulin levels
options.C: Excessive glucagon production by the liver
options.D: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells

explanation: Type 1 diabetes happens because the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h1)

question: A patient comes in with a metal flake stuck on the surface of their eye. Why is irrigation a good choice here?

options.A: Fluid pressure forces the metal deeper to hide the pain
options.B: Washing the eye replaces the need for a physical eye exam
options.C: Irrigation completely dissolves metal on contact
options.D: The fluid stream can safely flush away loose surface irritants

explanation: Spot on! If something is just resting loosely on the surface, a gentle, steady flow of liquid is a safe way to float it right out. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h2)

question: What does it mean when we say a nursing research problem must be empirically testable?

options.A: It requires no data collection from patients
options.B: It only relies on personal opinions and feelings
options.C: It has already been solved in past decades
options.D: The variables can be observed and measured

explanation: Empirical just means we can actually see, count, or measure it in the real world rather than just guessing or going purely on vibes! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why might older clinicians sometimes slow down the acceptance of new nursing practices?

options.A: They control the international accreditation of school curricula
options.B: They automatically receive higher salaries than reform advocates
options.C: They may prefer traditional workflows over new evidence-based guidelines
options.D: They are legally barred from entering modern hospital wards

explanation: Spot on! It's human nature to stick to what you are used to, so older staff can sometimes be hesitant with brand new routines. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following is a well-known online database used by nurses to find research?

options.A: Microsoft Paint
options.B: Adobe Reader
options.C: PubMed
options.D: Windows Explorer

explanation: PubMed is a primary online database providing free access to biomedical and nursing research literature. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which of these details is typically recorded in the stock inventory part of the safety form?

options.A: The personal home address of every patient
options.B: Opening balance and quantities used
options.C: Detailed medical diagnoses of injection recipients
options.D: Daily weather conditions at the facility

explanation: Correct! The stock section is strictly about numbers: what we started with, what we used, and what is left. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h3)

question: What does a "high-risk labour" mean for a mother and her baby?

options.A: A guarantee that a cesarean section is legally required
options.B: A pregnancy that requires no special medical supervision
options.C: An absolute certainty that the baby will be born premature
options.D: A greater chance of illness or death during childbirth

explanation: You've got this! High-risk labour just means there's an increased chance of complications for either mum or baby, so we need to keep our eyes open and stay extra vigilant. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h1)

question: Which of these is a great example of community-level disaster prep?

options.A: Clearing blocked drainage channels together before the rainy season begins
options.B: Relying entirely on federal radio broadcasts for weather updates
options.C: Waiting inside a flooded home for international rescue helicopters
options.D: Reporting abandoned buildings only after they collapse

explanation: Brilliant! Clearing drains together is a practical grassroots action that stops floods before the heavy rains even start. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why do we use the nursing process, especially in busy places like the ICU?

options.A: To replace the medical diagnosis made by the primary physician
options.B: To reduce the total number of nursing shifts required per week
options.C: To provide a systematic approach for individualized patient care
options.D: To eliminate the need for written nursing care plans

explanation: Think of the nursing process as your trusty roadmap! It helps you organize your thoughts and give care that is uniquely tailored to each patient's needs. You've got this! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h1)

question: What does the nursing abbreviation MSE stand for?

options.A: Medical Symptom Evaluation
options.B: Mental Stability Evaluation
options.C: Mental Status Examination
options.D: Mood State Estimator

explanation: MSE stands for Mental Status Examination. It's a quick, structured way nurses and doctors check how a patient is thinking, feeling, and functioning right now. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main difference between presumptive and probable signs of pregnancy?

options.A: Probable signs only show up right before birth
options.B: Presumptive signs are things the mother feels herself, while probable signs are things a nurse or doctor observes
options.C: Presumptive signs mean the baby is healthy, while probable signs mean trouble
options.D: Presumptive signs need lab tests, while probable signs need X-rays

explanation: Think of presumptive as what the client experiences (like nausea) and probable as what we find during our physical checks as clinicians! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T001#GNS226_U2_T001_h6)

question: What makes a histogram different from a regular bar chart?

options.A: The bars touch each other with no gaps
options.B: The bars are colored in bright shades
options.C: The chart includes a title at the top
options.D: The vertical axis measures percentages

explanation: Spot on! Bar charts have spaces between categories, but histograms touch because their numerical scale keeps right on going. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T9#GNS217_U4_T9_h3)

question: Four hours after a normal vaginal delivery, a mum hasn't peed yet, and her uterus feels soft (boggy) and pushed to the right. What is likely happening?

options.A: Sudden kidney failure caused by blood loss
options.B: A full bladder preventing the uterus from contracting
options.C: Normal postpartum diuresis filling the renal pelvis
options.D: Severe dehydration leading to low urine production

explanation: A full bladder acts like a roadblock, pushing the uterus out of place and stopping it from contracting properly. Always check the bladder if you notice a boggy uterus—it can prevent postpartum hemorrhage! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h6)

question: A nurse teaches primary school pupils about handwashing. Six weeks later, she checks if the rate of diarrhea among the children has dropped. What type of evaluation is this?

options.A: Financial budgeting
options.B: Impact evaluation
options.C: Logistical planning
options.D: Baseline assessment

explanation: Spot on! Looking at long-term health changes—like a drop in illness rates—tells you the real impact your teaching made. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why is it important for the family to have a direct contact number for the psychiatric ward during a patient's leave?

options.A: So they can order extra hospital meals to be delivered
options.B: So they can negotiate a discount on hospital bills
options.C: So they can seek immediate guidance before minor challenges escalate into major crises
options.D: So they can report local weather conditions to the doctor

explanation: Having a direct phone line gives families peace of mind and lets them get professional advice before small issues become big problems. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h7)

question: What key stage of a parasite's life cycle happens inside its definitive host?

options.A: The parasite reaches maturity and reproduces sexually
options.B: The parasite dies off because the immune system is too strong
options.C: The parasite transforms directly into an ectoparasite
options.D: The parasite only undergoes brief larval resting stages

explanation: You're doing great! The definitive host is the VIP lounge for the parasite—it's where they finally grow up into adults and reproduce. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h2)

question: Which type of equipment requires heavy capital funding in tertiary hospitals?

options.A: Simple mercury thermometers for home use
options.B: Basic paper record books and wooden furniture
options.C: Advanced diagnostic tools like CT scanners and dialysis machines
options.D: Manual hand fans for patient wards

options.A: The patient is intentionally trying to fake their injuries
options.B: A delayed infection is spreading through the bloodstream
options.C: Somatization translates emotional stress into physical symptoms
options.D: Standard hospital diagnostic machines are malfunctioning

explanation: Exactly! The mind and body are deeply connected. Emotional distress can show up as very real physical feelings like upset stomachs or tight chests—this is called somatization. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h2)

question: As a nurse, what is one of your main roles when it comes to nutrition and diet therapy?

options.A: Translating nutrition therapy into practical everyday habits for patients
options.B: Writing the definitive medical nutrition prescription for the hospital kitchen
options.C: Designing institutional food service menus for surgical wards
options.D: Diagnosing rare nutritional deficiencies using laboratory blood work

explanation: You are the vital link between doctor's orders and real life! Your job is to help patients take clinical nutrition advice and fit it smoothly into their daily meals and lifestyle. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h1)

question: When washing a patient's arms or legs during a bed bath, why does the nurse stroke from the hands or feet toward the torso?

options.A: To check if the patient has broken bones in the hand
options.B: To push all dirt and sweat directly into the armpits
options.C: To make the skin stretch out and look younger
options.D: To promote venous blood return toward the heart

explanation: Brilliant! Moving your washcloth upward helps push venous blood back up toward the heart against gravity, which is great for circulation. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h6)

question: If an unresponsive patient is taking slow, gasping, irregular breaths, how should a nurse respond?

options.A: As an indication to wait for natural breathing to stabilize
options.B: As a sign that the patient is recovering normal oxygen levels
options.C: As agonal respirations requiring immediate start of CPR
options.D: As proof that the airway is clear and no further action is needed

explanation: Don't let those gasps fool you! Agonal gasps are just a reflex when the heart stops. Treat them as cardiac arrest and start CPR right away. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which of these is counted as a healthy food group in standard dietary scoring?

options.A: Dark green leafy vegetables
options.B: Carbonated soft drinks

options.D: Artificial food flavorings

question: What do we call the time between when germs enter the body and when the first symptoms show up?

options.C: The brief moment when general fatigue starts
options.D: The final stage of complete body recovery

question: What is the medical term for an abnormally enlarged spleen?

options.A: Hepatomegaly
options.B: Lymphadenopathy
options.C: Cardiomegaly
options.D: Splenomegaly

question: Why must a healthcare plan include flexibility?

options.A: To allow staff to come to work whenever they feel like it.
options.B: To prevent the government from auditing the facility.
options.C: To handle unexpected clinical crises and emergencies smoothly.
options.D: To make it easier to change the hospital name and logo.

explanation: Medical environments change rapidly due to emergencies, requiring plans that can bend without breaking. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h4)

question: Who is considered a 'susceptible host'?

options.A: A patient who has complete immunity against all infections
options.B: An individual whose immune system cannot resist an invading pathogen
options.C: A person who currently carries a germ without symptoms
options.D: An object or surface where bacteria live and multiply

explanation: Right on! A susceptible host is simply someone whose body defense is low enough for germs to easily move in and cause sickness. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is most known for triggering dangerous heart rhythm changes?

options.A: Bicarbonate
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Sodium
options.D: Chloride

explanation: Potassium is a big deal for the heart! It directly helps maintain the electrical charge of heart cells. When potassium levels go out of whack, the heart's electrical system easily gets confused. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h2)

question: A patient is having a hard time buttoning their shirt and holding a toothbrush after a stroke. Who should step in to help with these daily tasks?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists are experts at helping patients regain fine motor skills for daily activities like dressing, eating, and brushing teeth. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h2)

question: A clinic has enough money for either a new blood-pressure machine or routine infant vaccines. As a public health nurse, what should you prioritize?

options.A: Save the money in a personal bank account until next year
options.B: The routine infant vaccines to prevent infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: Split the money evenly to buy broken office furniture
options.D: The blood pressure machine because adult patients complain more

explanation: Wonderful choice! Preventing deadly outbreaks in vulnerable infants always wins out because it protects the whole community's future. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h5)

question: What happens if a nurse wipes a disinfectant off a bedside table the very second after spraying it?

options.A: The chemical fails to achieve its required contact time, reducing germ kill rates
options.B: The active ingredients crystallize and become more potent over the next hour
options.C: The surface becomes completely sterile due to the sudden mechanical pressure

question: How do nursing leaders use the information gathered from emergency debriefing sessions?

options.A: To permanently reduce the number of emergency personnel on shift
options.B: To replace all clinical staff with automated computer systems
options.C: To justify cutting funding for emergency equipment stockpiles
options.D: To update disaster protocols, refine triage checklists, and guide staff training

explanation: Lessons learned from past emergencies directly translate into better guidelines, improved tools, and sharper training for healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h7)

question: When does continuous monitoring of a community mobilisation project take place?

options.A: Before entering the community for the first time
options.B: Throughout the implementation of the project

options.D: Never, because monitoring is unnecessary

explanation: Monitoring is an ongoing activity that happens while the project is running to ensure everything stays on track. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the FIRST thing you should do if a piece of equipment acts up while you are caring for a patient?

options.A: Remove the faulty item and replace it with a working one
options.B: Leave it plugged in so the next shift can look at it
options.C: Try to fix the internal wiring with electrical tape
options.D: Write an incident report for the hospital director

question: What does the term 'rheumatism' mean in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: An acute injury sustained during heavy physical labor
options.B: A single bacterial infection of the bone marrow
options.C: A complete degeneration of spinal discs from sudden trauma
options.D: Any painful condition affecting joints, muscles, or bones

explanation: Think of rheumatism as a helpful umbrella term! It covers various aches and pains in the musculoskeletal system rather than pointing to just one specific disease. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h1)

question: How do strong cultural preferences for traditional birth attendants usually affect postnatal referrals?

options.A: They ensure all newborn red flags are diagnosed early
options.B: They often cause dangerous delays in seeking formal medical care
options.C: They train primary health nurses in advanced surgical skills
options.D: They help finance hospital transport for emergency cases

question: Where does a water-soluble peptide hormone need to bind to send its message to a target cell?

options.A: Directly to DNA inside the cell nucleus
options.B: To a receptor on the outer cell membrane
options.C: To free-floating ribosomes in the cytoplasm
options.D: To transport proteins inside the blood vessel

question: How is gender mainly different from biological sex?

options.A: Gender remains identical across all human societies
options.B: Gender is based on social and cultural roles
options.C: Gender is determined strictly by genetics
options.D: Gender changes only with medical interventions

explanation: Spot on! While sex is biological, gender is all about the societal expectations, behaviors, and roles assigned to men and women, which can change depending on the culture. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T3#GNS312_U4_T3_h1)

question: What must form first before a bone can grow using endochondral ossification?

options.A: Primary vascular plexus
options.B: Hyaline cartilage model
options.C: Dense collagenous tendon
options.D: Fibrous connective tissue sheet

explanation: Think of cartilage as a tiny practice sculpture! Endochondral bones need a hyaline cartilage model first, which is later replaced by true bone. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T1#GNS121_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which contraceptive option is a long-acting reversible method placed right inside the uterus?

options.A: Combined oral pill
options.B: Emergency contraceptive pill

options.D: Intrauterine device

question: Why must nurses watch out for medication build-up in older adults receiving skilled care?

options.A: Renal and hepatic function always improve with advanced age.

options.C: Older adults process all drugs much faster than younger adults do.
options.D: Medications have no side effects once a patient enters a nursing home.

question: Which nursing action is an example of secondary prevention for a blood disorder?

options.A: Educating the community about eating iron-rich foods

question: What is the difference between allocative efficiency and technical efficiency?

options.A: Allocative efficiency deals with staff salaries, while technical efficiency deals with building construction
options.B: Allocative efficiency only applies to private clinics, while technical efficiency applies to government hospitals

question: Which of the following is NOT a known complication of intrapleural drug therapy?

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a symphysis joint in the body?

question: How can severe anxiety or fear slow down a mother's labour?

options.D: It causes the baby to immediately turn into a breech position.

question: What effect does severe maternal hypertension or pre-eclampsia typically have on foeto-placental exchange?

options.A: It makes the placental membrane thicker to block toxins

options.C: It reduces blood flow and decreases exchange efficiency

question: How do patients in strict isolation often feel emotionally?

question: What does a sudden spike in the incidence of a disease usually mean?

question: What is the purpose of the clean apron inside the home visiting kit?

question: Which nurse is usually on the frontline tracking daily infections on the hospital wards?

question: In Nigeria, what color of bin liner is normally used for ordinary, non-hazardous general waste?

question: How do modern nutritional guidelines differ from the ones created in the early 20th century?

question: How should a nurse properly document physical examination findings?

question: What is the main thing that sets a medical emergency apart from a trauma case?

question: What is the main job of the air-in-line detector on an infusion pump?

question: What is the name of the economic indicator used to measure a country's total output of goods and services?

question: What is the exact infectious stage of the parasite that actually enters the human body?

question: What popular model explains that errors happen when multiple system defenses fail all at once?

question: What is the main use of a daily vaccination tally sheet?

question: What is a common reason why patients stop taking their psychiatric medications?

question: What is the main focus of community-centred nursing care?

options.A: Promoting health within people's living environments

options.D: Treating severe illnesses inside hospital wards

question: Which of these is NOT a direct job of an antibody?

options.D: Neutralization of harmful bacterial toxins

question: What special feature in modern surgical swabs helps find them easily on an X-ray?

question: What is the big benefit of using an inhaler instead of pills for an asthma patient?

question: Which emergency shows up as facial swelling, upper body congestion, and swollen neck veins because a major blood vessel is blocked?

question: Which of the following is NOT true about integrating different types of healthcare plans?

question: What do we call a dangerously low level of oxygen in the blood?

question: Why can unending, chronic stress eventually lead to long-term anxiety or panic?

question: Why is clear documentation so important during patient transfers in a disaster?

question: Why is it important to involve traditional leaders and birth attendants in community maternal health programs?

question: Why is finding immunization defaulters so important for a community?

question: A low blood pressure warning pops up on your bedside monitor screen. Which computer cycle stage just happened?

question: When a baker uses yeast to make dough rise, which gas makes it happen?

question: A nurse wants to find out the percentage of pregnant women at a clinic who sleep less than five hours a night. Which design fits best?

question: A clinic nurse tests a urine sample from a 32-week pregnant woman and finds protein in it. What should the nurse suspect first?

question: Why do boat nurses need a wide, general set of nursing skills?
